Review: Exciting indoor maze experience for adults and children! Dynamic Maze finally lands in Jeju! It’s OK if you have physical muscular and intellectual strength! Now let’s face the volcanic island!

This is an excellent play place for teenagers. If you are a child 120 cm and under you must go with an adult. I recommend that if you’re really tall or big you might not want to go because this place has narrow tunnels. I almost got stuck in one of the hammock tunnels... haha.We saw this place on a pamphlet we got from the airport and really wanted to go right away and it was totally worth going.Remember to wear something comfortable because you’ll be moving around a lot so clothing with shenanigans hanging off from it probably won’t be a good idea. Or excessive jewelry. The price was 12000 per person for the Maze ep.3 and the Level 2 (harder level with timer) was around 5000?? But as a package it was 16000 per person. We had so much fun here!

While I was not able to scuba drive during my trip due to the weather the instructors were extremely friendly! They gave us their honest professional suggestion of alternative diving locations. They even went as far as recommending popular sites to visit during our trip that we would have never found without their help. I hope to visit again when the weather is optimal!

Jeju Shooting Range is Indoor pistol shooting range and holds a wide variety of handguns. In addition bibitan simulation shooting range operates with young children can enjoy together in a space. Thank you~

Great for both children and adults alike. Pistol shooting with live bullets only for adults and don?셳 forget to bring your ID/passport. Pretty pricey for 12 rounds but you can get a discount if you use the coupons from a Jeju Tourist Guidebook that you can get Jeju International Airport. For children there?셲 the shooting simulator available.

You need to present a copy of your identification before you are allowed into the range. At 35K Won it is not exactly the cheapest range in the world but it is cheaper than Seoul for sure.There are a variety of handguns to choose from and apart from the tacky advertisements on the wall it is actually quite a secure and well maintained range.Weapons are chained to the wall for safety and only the staff can tap you in or out. Good quality 3M earphones are used. There is also a selfie stick attached for you to take your pictures. Unfortunately the staff inside the range does not speak english (only the receptionist does basic english). However they do a pretty good job of demonstrating how to handle the weapon showing you on the screen where your shot have landed after each shot.After the shoot the receptionist will total up your score and pack your score sheet for you to bring it home as a souvenir. The hot tip is to book via Klook or Trazy and hunt for discounts instead of paying for the full price.Overall we enjoyed our shoot very much. Had it been cheaper we would definitely have another go.
This is my first shooting but I enjoyed a lot. It?셲 a small shooting rage but well organized. 35000 Won must be not expensive.

A waist of ??5000 to shoot 6 rounds with a pistol CHAINED to the wall. ??5000 for airsoft guns with messed up sights. And only kids 14 years and older. A waits look for Chained gun on YouTube in a few days.

Have never fired a live round before so this was pretty exhilarating for me. There are about 7-8 pistols and revolvers to choose from and i settled with a Beretta. There are computer screens that can help you to view where your last shot was. And at the end you can keep your target paper. We ate at the buffet downstairs on the 3rd floor before coming up as there is a 35% discount on the shooting range price after. The original price for 12 rounds is 35k won. The staff are not able to speak english at all which was quite a bummer as they will usually guide you and teach you how to shoot the target properly.

This place still exists as of April 2019. It's an amazing place for kids and they have so many toys and so much equipment. If your kids know about Tayo the little bus the place is magic and if they don't well it is still a pretty good kids play cafe. There's a cafe selling drinks and food. While as noted in the previous review the staffs English isn't good but is sufficient and they try to help. We have been to this Tayo cafe and some in Seoul as well. This one is much bigger and has more and better play equipment overall. It was also way less busy than the ones in Seoul and slightly cheaper @ 12k won per child and 3k won per adult compared to 15kw won per child and 5k won per adult in Seoul. Note: Visits are capped at 2 hours (or I'm sure the kids can play there all day)Tip: Ask the staff about riding the Tayo car ride as they are not always on but when you request a staff member will assist with it. Also the pork cutlet and rice were pretty decent for the kids (and adults) to eat.

A very fun place. My 1.5 to and 5yo enjoyed it very much. Reasonable priced (27000won for whole family play for 2 hours). Baby is free. A-must do thing for Tayo fans! Though not very English friendly. There's a cafeteria where you can eat and drink (you can ask for English menu). Staff are friendly. There are different colouring sheets of Tayo and friends that you can take for kids to colou

It was very far from what I expected and saw on photos they provided. I was outraged for what I got for $50. Frankly it ruined my experience in Jeju.

1. Everything (security instructions descriptions in the submarine) is in Korean/Chinese. Do not expect them to translate or be able to do so.

2. The submarine barely goes anywhere. It felt like we got into it moved 500m and stopped.

3. The place where we stopped was shallow and we couldn't see anything but rubbish and some algae.

4. What they do: they bring some fish (from container no natural fish there) to your window and take a photo of you with it (look point 5 about it). Do NOT expect to see real ocean WILD life.

5. SCAM: When you are boarding they will take a photo of you and say 'free photo included' but all photos except this one cost $5 each.

We expected all photos to be free (they told us so) thus allowed them to take photo when they brought fish to our window and we did not take photo on our devices. Thus we had to buy photos.

I had a great time doing this pheasant hunt and afterwards ate Pheasant Shabu Shabu. However there were some struggles in doing this trip which first of all - you must schedule an appointment with them at least 2 days prior to the day that you want to hunt it's quite pricey compared to other hunting opportunities that I've done (make sure you have a friend or you'll get charged the minimum of 2 people) it cannot rain a lot nor be really windy on the day of your hunt and lastly you have to at least have someone who speaks Korean well to get it scheduled. This last aspect is very important almost everywhere in Jeju as the people don't speak other languages - kind of like when my friend and I went fishing and scuba diving elsewhere on the island.So what happens on the day of the hunt? Well make sure you bring your passport and money to get the initial part out of the way. After that you start off with some shotgun practice (if you've never shot before then at least you get some warming up) then you jump on an ATV where you'll cruise to the hunting grounds and then head off to an area where it's setup like a Pheasant tower shoot except it's on the ground. I originally thought that we would have a hunting dog and walk around tracking down pheasants but that was not the case. They said that only happens during November-February when it's not hot. The shooting was very quick and we got all of our pheasants easily since I've hunted before and my friend and I have shotgunned before. Bring earplugs to the hunting grounds! They didn't provide any and I had a feeling that they wouldn't.Once we were done we took the ATVs back and went into the restaurant where they had everything setup for us minus the pheasant meat which they had to process. After boiling the broth for several minutes the meat came out and our server explained how to cook the meat which was great. You cannot beat fresh meat served to the dinner table like we did! It was so good that we skipped dinner because we ate a lot!Overall though I enjoyed it a lot because I was with my friend who had never hunted before. You must understand that there are a lot of people locals and tourists on the island of Jeju so it's not exactly the most open area out there for the best hunting and/or shooting opportunities available. They don't really openly market towards foreigners to show up but if more clients did show up then maybe they make some changes for the positive side. Pigs? Deer? Never know.This is a good place to take friends to enjoy something different especially for those who have never shot guns nor hunted before.

Daeyu Land offers skeet shooting and  quail hunting.   We went so my husband could try skeet shooting.   The location is at a gun club and has beautiful scenery.  For 35.00 you get a gun and 16 shots.   Unfortunately the shots only last about 10 minutes so a rather expensive activity.  It's easy to find off the main highway 1132.
Pheasant shabu shabu was surprisingly delicious and cooked very quickly.  Everyone said "it taste like chicken".
It cost 30+ thousand won for 12 clay shoots. There are also pistol shoots and ATV rides as well. The prices are really steep and we decided to give them a miss.

Husband and mate returned there 3 days in a row!!... You get skeet shooting but also real pheasant hunting.... they got 6 birds and invited the wives down to join them for lunch of shabu shabu with the pheasants they caught!!!  Nom Nom Nom

My husband and I had an absolutely fabulous day pheasant hunting at the Daeyoo Hunting Preserve on Jeju Island in South Korea and then an excellent meal of (our) pheasant sashimi roast pheasant etc. washed down with wine at their excellent pheasant restaurant! Daeyooland also has lovely gardens a charming helpful staff and great coffee!We hunted with a guide and his trusty dog walking for miles thru the beautiful countryside... and my husband did get us a pheasant! We also got to shoot skeet (and they have ATVing as well). My husband had hunted on Jeju many years ago when he was in the US Army and stationed in Korea and I wanted to take him "home" and go hunting with him- and tourists can hunt at Daeyooland! As their website is only in Korean our concierge at the JW Marriott in Seoul (an EXCELLENT hotel which I've also reviewed) was kind enough to help make the arrangements for us. We flew to Jeju Island for the day went hunting and then walked around downtown Jeju going to museums and some of the historic markets (there are 22!) buying and eating those famous Jeju oranges! Then we flew back to Seoul in the evening having had  a GREAT day!

Traveling and diving at Mun island which is a small island to the south of Jeju in the morning is a very refreshing experience. The scenery is beautiful and we saw a good amount of soft coral and school of fishes. Jen another instructor is also very helpful and it was fun chatting with her along the way. She gave me a ride and dropped me off at a local restaurant for lunch and the pork noodle she recommended was very delicious.
Did 2 tank dive lots of soft coral. Instructors spoke good English. Was safe and well trained. Gear was good too. Highly recommend if looking for a fun dive.

Staff were so kind and taught me in detail so that I could surf well. I took lessons three times here during the trip in Jeju and couldn't calm down as my current surfing skills leveled up. It was a totally exiting memory.

I visited here to experience the power of the waves as well as Korea's first surfing spot. As expected there were many people because it was a famous place but there were so many tourist attractions nearby that I could stay in nearby accommodations and experience various things. With Snoopy Garden’s steep entrance fee it initially didn’t make my itinerary. But the good reviews were consistent and friends also highly recommended the Charles Schulz’s Peanuts themed museum and garden. The indoor museum part was the highlight for me which had explanations about every main Peanuts character and several comic clips that span over Schulz’s 50 years of drawing them. The old newspaper clippings old toys and old books were also cool to look at. There are dozens of great photo spots which can create some major bottlenecks on crowded days. The garden had about half a dozen themed areas (including my favorite Charlie Brown’s baseball field) that are pretty vast and would have been a lot more pleasant to walk around in cooler weather. We skipped the cafe that charged a criminal 8500 won for a lemonade. I’m not sure that the high price of admission is justified but this is a well maintained attraction(which is refreshing considering the high number of run down museums and small theme parks in Jeju) and the quality of the displays are of superb quality. Adults and children both also fans and non-fans of Peanuts both would enjoy the visit here.

If you've never been to a Korean public bath then there are some things you should know. First go in and pay - currently it's 6000 Won for the baths (segregated by gender) and 8000 Won for both the bathes and the "jimjilbang" (which is a unisex area filled with different hot rooms to enjoy a sweat lodge style experience). You can stay as long as you want and even sleep there. I would never suggest doing so however since even though this is a standard option for most Korean baths and they are arguably the cheapest place to sleep in Korea they are also loud sometimes crowded and generally pretty damned uncomfortable for sleeping. You will be given a set of shorts and a shirt. If you are large like me you can expect to have to cram yourself into them. Use the key provided to find a locker in your respective undressing area. Don't worry even though it doesn't seem like you should be naked in this area it's okay.From here you will go into the showering/bathing area. DO NOT get into any of the pools without first scrubbing yourself down. Soap is provided as well as some abrasive washcloths but you will need your own shampoo which you can buy in the changing area. Once you are clean you can enjoy a variety of different temperature pools and sauna options ranging from the almost freezing to the almost boiling. After you are finished soaking you can either shower again and leave or put on the shorts provided and go to the jimjilbang common area. Here you will find several different hot rooms including a traditional mud hut style outside that looks like a giant wasps nest. Some of these rooms are intense so work your way up to the higher temperatures don't stay in for too long and remember to drink lots of water. Food and beverages will be available in the common area so remember to stash some cash in your shorts before going to the jimjilbang. You can also relax on the floors in the common area watching some bad TV or just snooze. There are a few other nooks and crannies you can explore but this is a basic sketch of what you can expect. Once you're done at the jimjilbang you can go back for another shower and soak dry off enjoy some complimentary personal hygiene products (although I urge caution with their aftershave) get dressed and go home.  Yongduamhaesu Land is a decent example of a Korean bath. It's fairly clean and has some nice facilities. It's also pretty busy so expect high volumes of people especially tourists. Oh and for all you "foreigners" out there of non-Asian decent please expect an awkward amount of interest in your body especially those regions that you'd rather not have a room full of Koreans staring at. I know this is weird and to be perfectly blunt I wish they could be more circumspect with their curiosity but they don't really mean any harm. It's an unspoken obsession amongst humans - particularly men and especially Korean men - to compare genitals. Koreans just tend to be more obvious about it in ways that might signal either sexual interest or a punch in the mouth in non-Korean cultures. Have patience.
